record.original_question: The number of k-power-free binary words of length n grows polynomially with n for k<= 7/3, but exponentially for k > 7/3 [39]. Examine analogous results for alphabets of arbitrary size.

evidence.quote: The number of k-power-free binary words of length n grows polynomially with n for k<= 7/3, but exponentially for k > 7/3 [39]. Examine analogous results for alphabets of arbitrary size.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_k = \{0, 1, \ldots, k-1\}$ be an alphabet of size $k \geq 2$. For a real number $\alpha > 1$, a finite word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n \in \Sigma_k^*$ is called an $\alpha$-power if it can be written as $w = u^p v$ where $u$ is a nonempty word, $p \geq 1$ is an integer, $v$ is a (possibly empty) prefix of $u$, and $|w|/|u| = \alpha$. A word is $\alpha$-power-free if none of its factors is a $\beta$-power for any $\beta \geq \alpha$. Let $L_k(\alpha, n)$ denote the number of $\alpha$-power-free words of length $n$ over $\Sigma_k$.

It is known that for $k = 2$ there exists a threshold $\alpha^*_2 = 7/3$ such that $L_2(\alpha, n)$ grows polynomially in $n$ for $\alpha \leq 7/3$ and exponentially in $n$ for $\alpha > 7/3$.

For each integer $k \geq 3$, determine the analogous polynomial-versus-exponential growth threshold $\alpha^*_k$, i.e., find the value $\alpha^*_k$ such that $L_k(\alpha, n)$ grows polynomially in $n$ for $\alpha \leq \alpha^*_k$ and exponentially in $n$ for $\alpha > \alpha^*_k$, and characterize the growth behavior at and around this threshold.
artifact.status_search_result: Considerable progress has been made for alphabets of size $k \geq 3$. Shur and others established asymptotic growth rates for $\beta$-power-free languages over $k$-letter alphabets, and a 2025 result (Dagstuhl/MFCS) proves Shur's conjecture on the exponential growth rates of $(k/(k-1))$-free and $(k/(k-1))^+$-free languages over large alphabets, with $O(1/k^2)$ corrections. The "exponential conjecture" (that for $k \geq 3$ all infinite power-free languages over $k$ letters have exponential size at the Dejean threshold) has been confirmed in several regimes. Thus the analogue of the binary 7/3 threshold is partially understood: the threshold is conjecturally the Dejean repetition threshold $k/(k-1)$, with strong supporting results, but a complete characterization for all $k$ matching the binary case is not fully settled.

status_evidence.title: A Proof of Shur's Conjecture on the Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Settles estimation of exponential growth rates of (n/(n-1))-free and (n/(n-1))^+-free languages over large alphabets with O(1/k^2) correction.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) progress confirming Shur's conjecture on growth rates over large alphabets.

status_evidence.title: Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies exponential growth rates of beta-power-free languages over k-letter alphabets; asymptotic formulas for beta >= 2.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic results on the polynomial-vs-exponential threshold for k-letter alphabets.

status_evidence.title: The Number of Threshold Words on n Letters Grows Exponentially
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that for n letters the number of threshold (Dejean-exponent) words grows exponentially.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms exponential growth at the Dejean threshold for many alphabet sizes.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial versus Exponential Growth in Repetition-Free Binary Words
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the 7/3 dividing line for binary power-free words.
status_evidence.claim: Reference for the binary case stated in the problem.
